blocks.text: Two weeks can cover many of Turkey's best-known places. Stay longer, and you can begin to travel differently.

Our 15+ day Turkey Tours can take you from Istanbul and Cappadocia through Ephesus and Pamukkale before continuing toward Bodrum, Antalya, Fethiye, and the Aegean or Mediterranean coast. On selected itineraries, part of the journey is spent aboard a traditional gulet rather than moving from one hotel to the next.

What is included depends on the route and can cover hotels, sightseeing with licensed English-speaking guides, airport transfers, domestic flights, entrance fees, ground transportation, and cruise accommodation where specified.
Private Tours and Customized Tours are available on selected extended itineraries.

sections.heading: What Changes When You Have 15 Days?

blocks.text: You can stop treating every extra day as an opportunity to add another destination.

On a shorter Turkey trip, domestic flights and carefully timed transfers help fit several regions into the available days. With 15 days or more, there is more room to stay longer, travel overland where it makes sense, and give the coastal part of the journey its own identity.
That can mean waking up in the same place for a second morning, spending an afternoon without scheduled sightseeing, or allowing the final part of the trip to feel different from the first.
For an extended Turkey tour, those details matter.

sections.heading: What Should the Coast Feel Like?

blocks.text: There are two quite different ways to finish a longer journey through Turkey.

One is to stay on land. A route through Bodrum, Antalya, Fethiye, or other coastal destinations keeps the familiar hotel-based structure while bringing the journey south toward the Aegean and Mediterranean.
The other is to leave the road behind for a while.

A Blue Cruise puts several nights of the coastal section aboard a traditional gulet. Instead of checking into another hotel after sightseeing, you travel by sea, stop in bays and coastal areas along the route, and sleep aboard the boat.
The destinations matter, but on a 15-day itinerary the way you travel through the coast can matter just as much.

sections.heading: Is a Blue Cruise Right for You?

blocks.text: A gulet is not simply another sightseeing excursion added to a Turkey tour.

You will be spending several days on a boat, so it is worth considering the experience itself. Cabins are different from hotel rooms, daily routines depend partly on the sailing program and conditions, and life aboard is naturally more informal.

For some travelers, that is exactly the point. After a first part of the trip filled with cities, archaeological sites, flights, and guided sightseeing, several days on the water can provide a welcome contrast.
Others would rather keep the flexibility and space of hotels while exploring the coast by land. In that case, a Bodrum, Antalya, or Fethiye-based route may be the better fit.

sections.heading: Don't Judge a Longer Tour by Its Stop Count

blocks.text: A 15-day itinerary with fewer destinations can sometimes offer more than one with a longer list.

Look at how many nights you spend in each place. Check where domestic flights are used and where the journey continues by road. If there is a Blue Cruise, see how many nights are actually aboard the gulet.
Also look for unscheduled time.

On an extended trip, a free afternoon or an extra night is not wasted space in the itinerary. After ten or twelve days of travelling, it can be one of the reasons the journey still feels enjoyable toward the end.

sections.heading: When Does the Coastal Season Matter?

blocks.text: It matters considerably if the coast or a Blue Cruise is an important part of your plans.
Late spring, summer, and early autumn are the natural periods for itineraries involving several days at sea. Exact cruise operations and sailing schedules depend on the season and individual program.

Spring and autumn also work particularly well when the first part of the journey includes extensive cultural sightseeing. Summer brings hotter conditions at archaeological sites but suits travelers who place greater emphasis on the coast and time on the water.
For an extended itinerary, choose the season for the whole journey, not only for Istanbul or Cappadocia.

sections.heading: Is a 15+ Day Turkey Tour for You?

blocks.text: Choose an extended itinerary because you want more time in Turkey, not because you feel obliged to see every major destination.

Fifteen days or more makes particular sense when the coast is an important part of the trip, when you want to include a genuine multi-night Blue Cruise, or when you simply prefer not to move at the pace required by a shorter circuit.
If your priorities are mainly Istanbul, Cappadocia, Ephesus, Pamukkale, and one additional region, you may find everything you need among our 10–14 Day Turkey Tour Packages.
For shorter routes, see our 6–9 Day Turkey Tour Packages, or return to the main Turkey Tours collection to compare the full range.

faqs.q: What can I expect from a 15-day Turkey tour?
faqs.a: A 15-day Turkey tour covers the full western circuit: Istanbul, Cappadocia, Troy, Pergamon, Ephesus, Pamukkale, Antalya, and Fethiye. It includes 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, the optional Cappadocia balloon flight, and the optional Blue Voyage gulet cruise on the Turquoise Coast. Domestic flights connect the inland and coastal sections.

faqs.q: Which destinations are included in 15-day Turkey itineraries?
faqs.a: Core destinations: Istanbul, Cappadocia (Goreme, Derinkuyu, Ihlara Canyon), Aegean coast (Troy, Pergamon, Ephesus, Pamukkale, Hierapolis), and the Riviera (Antalya, Fethiye, Oludeniz). Optional extensions available on longer programs: Trabzon and Sumela Monastery, Gaziantep and Gobeklitepe, Kars and Ani, Mount Ararat, and Lake Van.

faqs.q: How much does a 15-day Turkey tour cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Fifteen-day private tours cost approximately 3,000 to 4,500 USD per person based on double occupancy, depending on hotel category, domestic flight inclusions, and optional Blue Voyage. Small group fixed-date departures are typically 30 to 40 percent less per person. Contact us for a current quote.

faqs.q: Are all domestic flights included in 15+ day Turkey tours?
faqs.a: Yes. All domestic flights required by the itinerary are included: Istanbul to Kayseri (Cappadocia), Kayseri or Istanbul to Izmir (Aegean coast), and a return flight from Dalaman or Antalya to Istanbul. A separate domestic flight may be added for Eastern Turkey sections (Istanbul to Trabzon or Kars), which is included in extended program prices.

faqs.q: Is 15 days enough to explore Turkey fully?
faqs.a: Fifteen days covers the western and coastal Turkey circuit thoroughly. Eastern Turkey (Trabzon, Kars, Gobeklitepe, Mardin) adds 5 to 7 more days. Turkey has 21 UNESCO World Heritage Sites; a 15-day tour covers 4 to 5 of them. A truly comprehensive Turkey exploration requires 20 to 25 days.

faqs.q: What is Gobeklitepe and can it be added to a Turkey tour?
faqs.a: Gobeklitepe is a Neolithic temple complex near Sanliurfa in southeastern Turkey, built approximately 11,600 years ago. It is the oldest known example of monumental architecture in the world, predating Stonehenge by 6,000 years. It can be added to extended Turkey tours of 18 days or more as part of the southeastern circuit (Gaziantep, Sanliurfa, Gobeklitepe). It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (listed 2018).

faqs.q: Can I do a Blue Voyage on a 15-day Turkey tour?
faqs.a: Yes. The Blue Voyage is a natural component of 15-day tours that reach Fethiye. A 4-night gulet cruise from Fethiye replaces 4 hotel nights on the coast. Gulets sail to Butterfly Valley, the Twelve Islands, Oludeniz from the sea, and Gocek Bay. Private gulet charters are available for groups of 2 to 18 passengers.

faqs.q: Is Eastern Turkey safe to visit in 2026?
faqs.a: The major Eastern Turkey tourism destinations (Trabzon, Kars, Ani, Gaziantep, Sanliurfa, Mardin) are considered safe for tourists. Gobeklitepe receives over 600,000 visitors annually. The Mount Ararat summit attempt requires a permit obtained through a licensed operator. Magnificent Travel's guides have direct experience in all eastern regions and will confirm current conditions before departure

faqs.q: Can a 15+ day Turkey tour be combined with another country?
faqs.a: Yes. Turkey can be combined with Greece, Egypt, or Jordan after the Turkey circuit. However, a 15-day Turkey-only tour followed by another country requires at least 20 to 22 days total. For a combined itinerary that balances multiple countries, Turkey and Greece tours (10 to 14 days) or Turkey, Greece, and Egypt tours (16 to 19 days) are better suited.
